newsitem.title: CANADA: Westcoast finalizes incentive pipeline tolls.
newsitem.headline: Westcoast finalizes incentive pipeline tolls.

text.p: Westcoast Energy Inc said on Thursday it completed final agreements with natural gas shippers for an incentive toll arrangement and announced plans to expand its British Columbia pipeline system capacity.
Westcoast said it filed multi-year gathering, processing and transmission agreements with Canada's National Energy Board and expected them to be reviewed the week of June 23.
The incentive deals were signed with the Canadian Assiciation of Petroleum Producers, BC Gas Utility Ltd, Canwest Gas Supply, the Council of Canadian Forest Industries and the export Users Group.

The new arrangements, which would incorporate separate tolling mechanisms for the company's regulated pipeline system and its gathering and processing facilities, cover a five-year period starting January 1, 1997, Westcoast said.

Westcoast is the last major Canadian pipeline system to bring in incentive-based tolls, which offer pipeline companies and their customers opportunities to share the financial rewards from cost savings and new revenues.

Westcoast had been criticized by natural gas producers over the past few years as its system costs rose under the traditional tolling method while gas prices in British Columbia and its export points became depressed.

Some producers said the situation was forcing them to delay development plans in the province's northeast, one of Canada's most prospective gas regions. It also opened the door for new competitors to enter Westcoast's traditional British Columbia. turf.

"Pipeline system costs, and the regulatory treatment of these matters, have been a source of some uncertainty in northeast B.C. over the course of the last two years. The stage is now set to remove this issue," Westcoast Chairman Michael Phelps said in a statement.
"Strong commodity prices, significant exploration plans and market responsive policies will all serve to keep the natural gas industry very active in B.C."

Westcoast said the gathering and processing agreement would provide customers the option of signing contracts for one-, three- or five-year predetermined base tolls, plus a surcharge to be indexed monthly to gas prices.
Changes in contract levels for regulated gathering and processing facilities would not affect the tolls, the company said.

Also, base tolls in the deal would not include the recovery of development spending on the Grizzly Valley and Fort St. John gas plant expansions, it said. Cost recovery on the projects was slated to be the subject of a separate NEB hearing the same week.

The transmission agreement, meanwhile, would offer customers the choice of contracting for predetermined tolls for a five-year period or adjusted annually to reflect current costs and contracting levels, Westcoast said.
Westcoast also said on Thursday its pipeline division intended to hold an open season to determine market interest for an expansion of its transport capacity.
The system currently has capacity of about 2.2 billion cubic feet per day. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
